title: Mock approval gates accept a void under BLOCK and report can_release on ended deals
body:
## Summary
The browser mock (src/mock/backend.ts) diverges from Rust decide()/summary() on the approval window's money gates: deal_void succeeds under a shield BLOCK and can_release ignores terminal, replay and invoice deals.

## Description
Rust decide() (crates/table-runtime/src/service.rs:576-584) refuses every decision, void included, when deal.shield is BLOCK; the mock deal_void (apps/desktop/client/src/mock/backend.ts:938) checks only the state. Rust summary() sets can_release = configured && !locked && supported && !terminal && !MISMATCH && !BLOCK with supported excluding buyer non-purchase, invoice and replay deals (service.rs:426-490); the mock (backend.ts:837) has no !terminal and no invoice/replay exclusion. The client narrows these today (gating.ts ownsPaypalResource, and since 5c3d193 no void under BLOCK), so the demo cannot show a wrong button, but the mock is the only backend the client tests and the demo run against, and AGENTS.md says the mock's gates are never hand-edited away from the authority table.

## Flow
- mock: approval_summary on a replay purchase in AUTHORIZED -> can_release true (Rust: false)
- mock: deal_void on an AUTHORIZED deal with shield BLOCK -> VOIDED (Rust: INVALID)
- fix: mirror Rust's supported/terminal terms in can_release and refuse every decision under BLOCK in one shared mock guard

## Expected impact
Demo and client tests stop exercising transitions Rust refuses. Could break: demo scenarios that relied on a mock-only void.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the mock answers the approval gates as Rust does
Before: 1 of 7 decision commands accepted under BLOCK by the mock; can_release true on terminal/replay/invoice deals (read of backend.ts:837,938 vs service.rs)
After: predicted 0 of 7; can_release equal to Rust on the 21 states x 5 kinds x 2 sides grid
Method: simulation - read both implementations; src/mock is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
crates/table-runtime/src/service.rs:579-584 `|| deal.shield == Some(ShieldVerdict::Block) { return Err(invalid()); }`
apps/desktop/client/src/mock/backend.ts:938-942 deal_void: privileged, notWhileChecking, state AUTHORIZED -> VOIDED (no shield check)
apps/desktop/client/src/mock/backend.ts:837 can_release: !locked && configured && !buyerHaggle && shield !== BLOCK && state !== MISMATCH && (!rescue || rescueReleasable)
instrument: a vitest over createMockBackend: for each decision command on a BLOCK deal expect a refusal, and for the state x kind x side x mode grid expect can_release to equal a port of service.rs summary()'s formula

title: A failed refresh after the first read leaves the review looking current
body:
## Summary
Once a summary has loaded, DealReview keeps polling; a failed approval_summary sets loadError but the error renders only in the pre-summary branch, so the review keeps showing the last summary with no sign the wallet stopped answering.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/DealReview.tsx:90-99 sets loadError on a failed refetch; the only render of loadError is inside `if (!summary ...)` at DealReview.tsx:306. With a summary present the window keeps saying "Waiting for ..." or offering decisions from a summary that may be minutes old; only the in-browser phase shows a growing "checked N s ago". Rust re-checks every decision (checks_hash, terms_hash, attempt), so nothing wrong can move money, but the owner reads a stale state as current (async-ui-states: a failure must not render identically to success).

## Flow
- the wallet actor stops while the approval window shows a deal
- poll -> approval_summary rejects UNAVAILABLE -> loadError set
- the footer shows no notice; the says line, steps and buttons are the last good read

## Expected impact
The owner learns the wallet is unreachable before pressing a button rather than from a refusal after it. Could break: a transient poll failure flashes a notice (clear it on the next good read).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a failed refresh is visible
Before: loadError rendered in 1 of 2 branches (no summary yet); with a summary, 0 notices on a failed poll (read of DealReview.tsx:90-99, 293-310, 503-505)
After: predicted: a footerNoticeText(read) notice while loadError is set and a summary is shown, cleared on the next successful read
Method: simulation - three walked cases (wallet stopped, ledger trust failure, window permission lost); a render test of DealReview needs a mocked runtime and the session/handoff hooks, which the round did not build
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a DealReview render test with lib/runtime mocked: approval_summary resolves once then rejects UNAVAILABLE; advance the 10 s poll; expect a notice carrying footerNoticeText(read) and no raw message

title: The type-the-name step before unpausing a scam-check hold is enforced only in the window
body:
## Summary
Releasing a shield HOLD asks the owner to type the payee's name exactly; Rust's shield_release takes DecisionArgs with no name, so the friction is a client-only narrowing any other caller of the command skips.

## Description
gating.ts:187-192 enables releaseHold only when namesMatch(typed, expectedName); DealReview.tsx:480-501 renders the typer. crates/table-runtime/src/service.rs decide(ReleaseHold) checks token, label, unlock, selection, terms, attempt and the checklist (shield line exempt) but receives no typed name (bindings/DecisionArgs.ts has deal_id, attempt, terms_hash, checks_hash, counter_hash). The approval window is the only UI that holds the capability, so the gap is defence in depth, not an open door. Enforcing it in Rust means a new DecisionArgs field and an authority/binding change (AGENTS.md IPC procedure), and deciding whether the name check is a security control or a UX speed bump is the owner's call.

## Flow
- owner opens a HOLD deal; window requires the typed name
- a privileged shield_release call with valid DecisionArgs and no name is accepted by Rust
- option: add typed_name to the release args and compare it in decide(ReleaseHold) against the counterparty display

## Expected impact
Makes the confirmation a property of the wallet, not of one page. Could break: every caller and the mock must send the name; PINNED_MANIFEST unchanged (args, not authority).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the release confirmation is enforced where the decision is made
Before: typed-name check on 1 of 2 layers (client only)
After: predicted 2 of 2
Method: simulation - read gating.ts, DealReview.tsx and service.rs decide(); a contract change was out of this round's scope
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/gating.ts:191 `(namesMatch(ctx.typedName, ctx.expectedName) ? null : ...)`
crates/table-runtime/src/service.rs:653-657 Decision::ReleaseHold => record + owner_release_hold(deal.id, args.attempt, ticket, now) (no name)

title: Bound the CHECKING reveal by the row count instead of a fixed 8 ticks
body:
## Summary
DealReview's reveal interval stops after 8 ticks; a comparison with more than 8 rows would never finish CHECKING and keep every money button disabled.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/DealReview.tsx:186-191 clears the interval when i > 7; allRevealed needs revealed >= max(rowCount, checks.length). buildDiff returns at most 6 rows (accept 6, approve 6, capture 6, hold 5, lever 5, review 4) and the checklist has 6 ids, so no reachable input fails today.

## Flow
- count rows per diff kind in review/diff.ts
- compare with the 8-tick cap

## Expected impact
None today.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the reveal always completes
Before: 0 reachable inputs stall (max 6 rows, 6 checks vs cap 8)
After: 0
Method: probe - counted every buildDiff branch and ApprovalCheckId
Result: not-better
Gate: none
